parameters.content:
## Module 2 — Technical content generation

Five stages, not one agent.

**A5 — Build Proposal Config** (deterministic). Resolves schemas/chapter-catalog.json
against this request (tier, scope, pricing) and against the client's *Proposal Config*
Google Sheet: which chapters, renamed how, plus their clause library and writing rules.
Clause selection is a token matcher, never an LLM — this node decides which warranty and
liability text goes out.

**A1 → A2 → A3** write the generated 30-35%. Sequential, not parallel: the execution plan
has to match the architecture, and the executive summary has to summarise both. Each has
its own token budget (the old single call had 8192 for the whole document).

**A4 — QA Review** reads the assembled draft: contradictions between chapters, invented
commitments, uncovered RFQ requirements. It may patch generated sections; boilerplate is
read-only and a patch aimed at one becomes a finding.

Boilerplate never passes through a model. It goes from the client's spreadsheet to the
render context directly — see modules/proposal/render_context.js.

// === CHAPTER CATALOG CORE START ===

// The catalog itself. A Code node cannot read files, so `node scripts/mirror-cores.js` replaces
// the block between these two markers with the inlined contents of the JSON when it copies this
// core into n8n. Everything else is identical on both sides.
const CHAPTER_CATALOG = {
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "$id": "https://cifral.io/schemas/chapter-catalog.json",
  "title": "Cifral — Proposal chapter catalog",
  "description": "The canonical, versioned superset of chapters a Cifral proposal can contain. This is the CLOSED VOCABULARY shared by the Module 2 agents, the render context (modules/proposal/render_context.js) and the .docx template tags — an id that is not in here has no agent that knows how to write it and no template block to render it. Per-client customization does NOT happen in this file: it happens in the client's 'Proposal Config' Google Sheet (docs/CLIENT-DRIVE-SETUP.md), which selects, reorders, renames and supplies text OVER this vocabulary. Same split as pricing: the repo owns the formula, Drive owns the numbers. Every chapter id and section id is also a RENDER KEY: it produces {#has_<id>}, {#<id>.parrafos} and {#<id>.bullets} in the template, exactly like the seven narrative sections did before. Ids must be valid Jexl identifiers — ASCII, lowercase, underscores only, no accents and no '-' (Jexl reads '-' as subtraction).",
  "version": 1,

  "tiers": {
    "A": { "label": { "es": "Cotización", "en": "Quotation" }, "pages": "4-8" },
    "B": { "label": { "es": "Propuesta estándar", "en": "Standard proposal" }, "pages": "15-25" },
    "C": { "label": { "es": "Licitación", "en": "Tender" }, "pages": "30-60 + anexos" }
  },

  "agents": {
    "A1": { "role": { "es": "Ingeniería / solución técnica", "en": "Engineering / technical solution" } },
    "A2": { "role": { "es": "Ejecución y planificación", "en": "Execution and planning" } },
    "A3": { "role": { "es": "Comercial / ejecutivo", "en": "Commercial / executive" } },
    "A4": { "role": { "es": "Revisor QA (no escribe capítulos)", "en": "QA reviewer (writes no chapters)" } },
    "A5": { "role": { "es": "Selector de cláusulas (motor de reglas determinista)", "en": "Clause selector (deterministic rules engine)" } }
  },

  "content_types": {
    "generated": "Written by an LLM agent, specific to this project.",
    "boilerplate": "Selected from the client's clause library (Proposal Config sheet, tab 'Content'). Never LLM-written — this is contract text.",
    "calculated": "Derived deterministically from RFQ / pricing data. Never LLM-written.",
    "mixed": "A generated body plus boilerplate clauses merged into the same paragraph stream."
  },

  "front_matter": [
    { "id": "portada", "order": 1, "numbered": false, "title": { "es": "Portada", "en": "Cover" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "content_type": "calculated", "agent": null, "requires_scope": [], "sections": [], "tables": [] },
    { "id": "carta_presentacion", "order": 2, "numbered": false, "default_included": false, "title": { "es": "Carta de presentación", "en": "Cover letter" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "content_type": "generated", "agent": "A3", "requires_scope": [], "sections": [], "tables": [] },
    { "id": "control_version", "order": 3, "numbered": false, "title": { "es": "Control de versión", "en": "Version control" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "content_type": "calculated", "agent": null, "requires_scope": [], "sections": [], "tables": ["tabla_versiones"] },
    { "id": "indice", "order": 4, "numbered": false, "title": { "es": "Índice", "en": "Table of contents" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "content_type": "calculated", "agent": null, "requires_scope": [], "sections": [], "tables": ["tabla_indice"] },
    { "id": "glosario", "order": 5, "numbered": false, "title": { "es": "Glosario y abreviaturas", "en": "Glossary and abbreviations" }, "tiers": ["C"], "content_type": "boilerplate", "agent": "A5", "requires_scope": [], "sections": [], "tables": ["tabla_glosario"] }
  ],

  "chapters": [
    {
      "id": "resumen_ejecutivo",
      "order": 10,
      "numbered": true,
      "title": { "es": "Resumen ejecutivo", "en": "Executive summary" },
      "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"],
      "content_type": "generated",
      "agent": "A3",
      "requires_scope": [],
      "guidance": "Must read standalone: someone who reads only this page knows what is being bought, why, what it costs and when it lands. No jargon, no acronyms without expansion, client's language not ours. Written LAST, from A1+A2 output.",
      "tables": [],
      "sections": [
        { "id": "resumen_ejecutivo_necesidad", "title": { "es": "La necesidad", "en": "The need" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "resumen_ejecutivo_solucion", "title": { "es": "La solución propuesta", "en": "The proposed solution" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "resumen_ejecutivo_beneficios", "title": { "es": "Beneficios e indicadores", "en": "Benefits and KPIs" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": ["tabla_beneficios"] },
        { "id": "resumen_ejecutivo_economico", "title": { "es": "Resumen económico y plazo", "en": "Commercial and schedule summary" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "content_type": "calculated", "tables": [] }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "bases_oferta",
      "order": 20,
      "numbered": true,
      "title": { "es": "Bases de la oferta", "en": "Basis of offer" },
      "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"],
      "content_type": "mixed",
      "agent": "A5",
      "requires_scope": [],
      "guidance": "What this offer is built on. Reference documents must be dated and revision-stamped — this is what protects against 'but the spec said'.",
      "tables": [],
      "sections": [
        { "id": "bases_oferta_documentos", "title": { "es": "Documentos de referencia", "en": "Reference documents" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "tables": ["tabla_documentos_ref"] },
        { "id": "bases_oferta_normativa", "title": { "es": "Normativa y estándares aplicables", "en": "Applicable standards and regulations" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": ["tabla_normativa"] },
        { "id": "bases_oferta_premisas", "title": { "es": "Premisas generales", "en": "General assumptions" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "tables": [] }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "antecedentes",
      "order": 30,
      "numbered": true,
      "title": { "es": "Antecedentes y situación actual", "en": "Background and current situation" },
      "tiers": ["B", "C"],
      "content_type": "generated",
      "agent": "A3",
      "requires_scope": [],
      "guidance": "Prove we understood the problem before proposing anything. Quantify the pain with the client's own numbers (downtime, obsolescence, spares lead time). Never invent figures the RFQ did not provide.",
      "tables": [],
      "sections": [
        { "id": "antecedentes_instalacion", "title": { "es": "Instalación existente", "en": "Existing installation" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "antecedentes_problematica", "title": { "es": "Problemática y obsolescencia", "en": "Problem statement and obsolescence" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "antecedentes_objetivos", "title": { "es": "Objetivos y criterios de éxito", "en": "Objectives and success criteria" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "solucion_tecnica",
      "order": 40,
      "numbered": true,
      "title": { "es": "Solución técnica propuesta", "en": "Proposed technical solution" },
      "tiers": ["B", "C"],
      "content_type": "generated",
      "agent": "A1",
      "requires_scope": ["materials", "engineering"],
      "guidance": "The engineering argument. Architecture first, then what physically changes, then how it is controlled. Name component categories, never invent brands, part numbers or performance figures.",
      "tables": [],
      "sections": [
        { "id": "solucion_tecnica_arquitectura", "title": { "es": "Concepto y arquitectura", "en": "Concept and architecture" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "solucion_tecnica_funcional", "title": { "es": "Descripción funcional y cambios respecto a la instalación actual", "en": "Functional description and changes to the existing installation" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "solucion_tecnica_control", "title": { "es": "Control y comunicaciones", "en": "Control and communications" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "solucion_tecnica_ciberseguridad", "title": { "es": "Ciberseguridad OT y acceso remoto", "en": "OT cybersecurity and remote access" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "solucion_tecnica_alternativas", "title": { "es": "Alternativas evaluadas y justificación", "en": "Alternatives considered and rationale" }, "tiers": ["C"], "tables": ["tabla_alternativas"] }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "alcance_suministro",
      "order": 50,
      "numbered": true,
      "title": { "es": "Alcance de suministro", "en": "Scope of supply" },
      "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"],
      "content_type": "generated",
      "agent": "A1",
      "requires_scope": [],
      "guidance": "DELIVERABLES ONLY — what physically or digitally changes hands. Everything about HOW it gets done belongs in 'ejecucion'. Procurement reads this line by line against the tender, so be enumerable, not narrative.",
      "tables": [],
      "sections": [
        { "id": "alcance_suministro_resumen", "title": { "es": "Resumen de lo incluido y no incluido", "en": "Summary of what is and is not included" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "content_type": "calculated", "tables": [] },
        { "id": "alcance_suministro_hardware", "title": { "es": "Hardware y equipos", "en": "Hardware and equipment" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "requires_scope": ["materials"], "tables": ["tabla_materiales"] },
        { "id": "alcance_suministro_software", "title": { "es": "Software y licencias", "en": "Software and licences" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "alcance_suministro_scada", "title": { "es": "SCADA / HMI y visualización", "en": "SCADA / HMI and visualisation" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "alcance_suministro_ingenieria", "title": { "es": "Ingeniería y diseño", "en": "Engineering and design" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "requires_scope": ["engineering"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "alcance_suministro_recambios", "title": { "es": "Recambios recomendados", "en": "Recommended spare parts" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "requires_scope": ["spare_parts"], "tables": ["tabla_recambios"] },
        { "id": "alcance_suministro_documentacion", "title": { "es": "Documentación técnica entregable", "en": "Technical documentation deliverables" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "content_type": "boilerplate", "agent": "A5", "tables": [] }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "ejecucion",
      "order": 60,
      "numbered": true,
      "title": { "es": "Ejecución del proyecto", "en": "Project execution" },
      "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"],
      "content_type": "generated",
      "agent": "A2",
      "requires_scope": [],
      "guidance": "SERVICES ONLY — how the deliverables get installed, tested and handed over. Engineering evaluates risk here, so be concrete about sequence, duration and who does what.",
      "tables": [],
      "sections": [
        { "id": "ejecucion_inspeccion", "title": { "es": "Inspección previa y toma de datos", "en": "Site survey and data capture" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "ejecucion_fases", "title": { "es": "Fases de ejecución", "en": "Execution phases" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "tables": ["tabla_fases"] },
        { "id": "ejecucion_instalacion", "title": { "es": "Instalación y montaje", "en": "Installation and assembly" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "requires_scope": ["installation"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "ejecucion_puesta_marcha", "title": { "es": "Puesta en marcha", "en": "Commissioning and start-up" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "requires_scope": ["commissioning"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "ejecucion_pruebas", "title": { "es": "Plan de pruebas y criterios de aceptación", "en": "Test plan and acceptance criteria" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": ["tabla_pruebas"] },
        { "id": "ejecucion_demostracion", "title": { "es": "Periodo de demostración", "en": "Demonstration period" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "ejecucion_formacion", "title": { "es": "Formación", "en": "Training" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "requires_scope": ["training"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "ejecucion_transporte", "title": { "es": "Transporte, embalaje y entrega", "en": "Transport, packing and delivery" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "requires_scope": ["shipping"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "ejecucion_recepcion", "title": { "es": "Recepción y aceptación", "en": "Handover and acceptance" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "content_type": "boilerplate", "agent": "A5", "tables": [] }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "gestion_proyecto",
      "order": 70,
      "numbered": true,
      "title": { "es": "Gestión de proyecto", "en": "Project management" },
      "tiers": ["B", "C"],
      "content_type": "mixed",
      "agent": "A2",
      "requires_scope": [],
      "guidance": "How the project is run and controlled. The schedule lives here even when project management is out of scope — the client always needs to know when things land.",
      "tables": [],
      "sections": [
        { "id": "gestion_proyecto_organizacion", "title": { "es": "Organización y equipo", "en": "Organisation and team" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "requires_scope": ["project_management"], "tables": ["tabla_equipo"] },
        { "id": "gestion_proyecto_metodologia", "title": { "es": "Metodología y control del proyecto", "en": "Methodology and project control" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "content_type": "boilerplate", "agent": "A5", "tables": [] },
        { "id": "gestion_proyecto_comunicacion", "title": { "es": "Comunicación y reporting", "en": "Communication and reporting" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "content_type": "boilerplate", "agent": "A5", "tables": [] },
        { "id": "gestion_proyecto_cambios", "title": { "es": "Gestión de cambios", "en": "Change management" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "content_type": "boilerplate", "agent": "A5", "tables": [] },
        { "id": "gestion_proyecto_calidad", "title": { "es": "Calidad y plan de puntos de inspección", "en": "Quality and inspection test plan" }, "tiers": ["C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "gestion_proyecto_planificacion", "title": { "es": "Planificación, hitos y plazo", "en": "Schedule, milestones and lead time" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": ["tabla_hitos"] }

    },
    {

      "agent": "A2",

      "guidance": "THE brownfield differentiator. The client's number one fear is 'will you stop my plant'. Answer it explicitly: what keeps running, what the fallback is if a step fails, how the old system stays available until the new one is proven.",

      "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"],

      "agent": "A5",

      "tables": [],
      "sections": [

        { "id": "limites_alcance_interfaces", "title": { "es": "Interfaces y límites de suministro", "en": "Interfaces and battery limits" }, "tiers": ["B", "C"], "tables": [] },
        { "id": "limites_alcance_cambios", "title": { "es": "Condiciones que originan una orden de cambio", "en": "Conditions triggering a change order" }, "tiers": ["A", "B", "C"], "tables": [] }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "oferta_economica",

const TIER_RANK = { A: 0, B: 1, C: 2 };

function normText(v) {
  return v == null ? '' : String(v).trim();
}

function truthy(v) {
  const s = normText(v).toLowerCase();
  if (!s) return null; // empty means "inherit", not "no"
  return ['1', 'true', 'yes', 'si', 'sí', 'x', 'y'].includes(s);
}

function pickLang(v) {
  return v === 'es' ? 'es' : 'en';
}

/**
 * Parse one `applies_when` cell into a predicate description.
 *
 * Deliberately NOT a DSL and never eval'd: this string is typed by a salesperson into a
 * spreadsheet, and it decides which contract text goes out. Tokens are comma-separated and
 * ALL must match. Anything unrecognised is reported as a warning and treated as "does not
 * match", so a typo silently drops one clause instead of silently applying all of them.
 *
 *   (empty) | always            -> always applies
 *   scope:installation          -> that scope item is true for this request
 *   tier:B  |  tier:B+          -> exactly tier B  |  tier B or above
 *   lang:es                     -> proposal language
 *   country:ES                  -> project country
 *   pricing | no_pricing        -> whether the request carries a price
 */
function matchesApplies(raw, ctx, warnings, label) {
  const text = normText(raw).toLowerCase();
  if (!text || text === 'always') return true;

  for (const token of text.split(',')) {
    const t = token.trim();
    if (!t) continue;
    const [key, valRaw] = t.split(':');
    const val = normText(valRaw).toLowerCase();

    if (key === 'always') continue;
    else if (key === 'pricing') { if (!ctx.has_pricing) return false; }
    else if (key === 'no_pricing') { if (ctx.has_pricing) return false; }
    else if (key === 'scope') { if (!ctx.scope[val]) return false; }
    else if (key === 'lang') { if (ctx.language !== val) return false; }
    else if (key === 'country') { if (normText(ctx.country).toLowerCase() !== val) return false; }
    else if (key === 'tier') {
      const plus = val.endsWith('+');
      const want = (plus ? val.slice(0, -1) : val).toUpperCase();
      if (!(want in TIER_RANK)) { warnings.push(`${label}: unknown tier '${want}' in applies_when`); return false; }
      if (plus ? TIER_RANK[ctx.tier] < TIER_RANK[want] : ctx.tier !== want) return false;
    } else {
      warnings.push(`${label}: unknown applies_when token '${t}'`);
      return false;
    }
  }
  return true;
}

// A chapter/section survives when its tier includes the document tier AND, if it declares
// requires_scope, at least one of those scope items is in scope for this request.
function passesGates(entry, ctx) {
  const tiers = Array.isArray(entry.tiers) ? entry.tiers : ['A', 'B', 'C'];
  if (!tiers.includes(ctx.tier)) return false;
  const req = Array.isArray(entry.requires_scope) ? entry.requires_scope : [];
  if (req.length && !req.some((k) => ctx.scope[k])) return false;
  if (entry.gated_by === 'has_pricing' && !ctx.has_pricing) return false;
  return true;
}

// Rows of the sheet's `Rules` tab -> the rules object injected into the agent prompts.
function buildRules(rows) {
  const rules = { terminology: {} };
  const LIST_KEYS = ['forbidden_words', 'must_mention'];
  for (const r of rows || []) {
    const key = normText(r.key);
    const value = normText(r.value);
    if (!key) continue;
    if (key.toLowerCase().startsWith('term:')) {
      rules.terminology[key.slice(5).trim()] = value;
    } else if (LIST_KEYS.includes(key)) {
      rules[key] = value ? value.split(',').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean) : [];
    } else if (['warranty_months', 'validity_days'].includes(key)) {
      const n = Number(value);
      if (Number.isFinite(n)) rules[key] = n;
    } else {
      rules[key] = value;
    }
  }
  return rules;
}

// Rows of the sheet's `Chapters` tab -> per-chapter overrides, keyed by chapter/section id.
function buildOverrides(rows, warnings, knownIds) {
  const map = {};
  for (const r of rows || []) {
    const id = normText(r.chapter_id);
    if (!id) continue;
    if (knownIds && !knownIds.has(id)) {
      warnings.push(`Chapters tab: unknown chapter_id '${id}' — no such chapter in the catalog, row ignored`);
      continue;
    }
    map[id] = {
      include: truthy(r.include),
      order: r.order === '' || r.order == null ? null : Number(r.order),
      title_es: normText(r.title_es),
      title_en: normText(r.title_en),
      tier: normText(r.tier).toUpperCase() || null,
    };
  }
  return map;
}

function titleFor(entry, override, lang) {
  const fromSheet = override && (lang === 'es' ? override.title_es : override.title_en);
  if (fromSheet) return fromSheet;
  const t = entry.title || {};
  return normText(t[lang]) || normText(t.en) || normText(t.es) || entry.id;
}

function collectIds(catalog) {
  const ids = new Set();
  for (const group of ['front_matter', 'chapters', 'annexes']) {
    for (const ch of catalog[group] || []) {
      ids.add(ch.id);
      for (const s of ch.sections || []) ids.add(s.id);
    }
  }
  return ids;
}

/**
 * Resolve the catalog against one client's sheet and one request.
 *
 * `sheet` is the raw read of the three tabs ({chapters, content, rules}), or null when the
 * client has no Proposal Config sheet — in which case the catalog defaults are used and
 * everything still works. That fallback is what keeps existing clients from breaking when
 * this ships.
 */
function resolveProposalConfig({ catalog, sheet, tier, language, scope, has_pricing, country, sheet_id }) {
  const warnings = [];
  const lang = pickLang(language);
  const rules = buildRules(sheet && sheet.rules);

  const wantTier = normText(tier).toUpperCase() || normText(rules.default_tier).toUpperCase() || 'B';
  const resolvedTier = wantTier in TIER_RANK ? wantTier : 'B';
  if (!(wantTier in TIER_RANK)) warnings.push(`Unknown tier '${wantTier}', falling back to 'B'`);

  const ctx = {
    tier: resolvedTier,
    language: lang,
    scope: scope || {},
    has_pricing: !!has_pricing,
    country: country || '',
  };

  const knownIds = collectIds(catalog);
  const overrides = buildOverrides(sheet && sheet.chapters, warnings, knownIds);

  // --- select ---------------------------------------------------------------
  const groups = [
    ['front_matter', catalog.front_matter || []],
    ['body', catalog.chapters || []],
    ['annex', catalog.annexes || []],
  ];

  const selected = [];
  for (const [group, entries] of groups) {
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const ov = overrides[entry.id];
      // include: explicit sheet value wins; otherwise the catalog default; otherwise the gates.
      const explicit = ov ? ov.include : null;
      if (explicit === false) continue;
      if (explicit !== true) {
        if (entry.default_included === false) continue;
        if (!passesGates(entry, ctx)) continue;
      }

      const sections = [];
      for (const s of entry.sections || []) {
        const sov = overrides[s.id];
        const sExplicit = sov ? sov.include : null;
        if (sExplicit === false) continue;
        if (sExplicit !== true) {
          if (s.default_included === false) continue;
          if (!passesGates({ tiers: s.tiers || entry.tiers, requires_scope: s.requires_scope, gated_by: s.gated_by }, ctx)) continue;
        }
        sections.push({
          id: s.id,
          title: titleFor(s, sov, lang),
          content_type: s.content_type || entry.content_type || 'generated',
          agent: s.agent !== undefined ? s.agent : (entry.agent || null),
          tables: Array.isArray(s.tables) ? s.tables : [],
        });
      }

      selected.push({
        id: entry.id,
        group,
        order: ov && ov.order != null && Number.isFinite(ov.order) ? ov.order : entry.order,
        numbered: entry.numbered,
        title: titleFor(entry, ov, lang),
        content_type: entry.content_type || 'generated',
        agent: entry.agent !== undefined ? entry.agent : null,
        guidance: normText(entry.guidance),
        tables: Array.isArray(entry.tables) ? entry.tables : [],
        sections,
      });
    }
  }

  selected.sort((a, b) => (a.order - b.order) || a.id.localeCompare(b.id));

  // --- number ---------------------------------------------------------------
  // Numbers are assigned AFTER exclusions, so a dropped chapter leaves no gap. Word's
  // multilevel list does the same thing for the visible headings; these values exist for the
  // table of contents and for cross-references in the text.
  let bodyN = 0;
  let annexN = 0;
  const ALPHA = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ';
  for (const ch of selected) {
    if (ch.group === 'body') {
      bodyN += 1;
      ch.numero = String(bodyN);
    } else if (ch.group === 'annex') {
      ch.numero = ALPHA[annexN] || `A${annexN}`;
      annexN += 1;
    } else {
      ch.numero = '';
    }
    ch.sections.forEach((s, i) => {
      s.numero = ch.numero ? `${ch.numero}.${i + 1}` : '';
    });
  }

  // --- clauses --------------------------------------------------------------
  const renderedIds = new Set();
  for (const ch of selected) {
    renderedIds.add(ch.id);
    for (const s of ch.sections) renderedIds.add(s.id);
  }

  const clauses = [];
  const VALID_KINDS = ['clause', 'exclusion', 'premise', 'obligation', 'term'];
  for (const r of (sheet && sheet.content) || []) {
    const id = normText(r.id);
    const chapter_id = normText(r.chapter_id);
    const body = normText(r.body);
    if (!id && !body) continue;

    const kind = (normText(r.kind) || 'clause').toLowerCase();
    if (!VALID_KINDS.includes(kind)) { warnings.push(`Content tab: row '${id}' has unknown kind '${kind}', ignored`); continue; }
    const rowLang = normText(r.lang).toLowerCase();
    if (rowLang && rowLang !== lang) continue;
    if (!body) { warnings.push(`Content tab: row '${id}' has an empty body, ignored`); continue; }
    if (!knownIds.has(chapter_id)) { warnings.push(`Content tab: row '${id}' points at unknown chapter_id '${chapter_id}', ignored`); continue; }
    if (!matchesApplies(r.applies_when, ctx, warnings, `Content tab row '${id}'`)) continue;
    // A clause attached to a chapter this request does not render is not an error — the
    // client keeps clauses for scopes they are not selling today.
    if (!renderedIds.has(chapter_id)) continue;

    clauses.push({ kind, id, chapter_id, lang, title: normText(r.title), body, applies_when: normText(r.applies_when) });
  }

  return {
    source: sheet ? 'sheet' : 'catalog_default',
    sheet_id: sheet_id || null,
    tier: resolvedTier,
    language: lang,
    chapters: selected,
    clauses,
    rules,
    // The COMPLETE catalog vocabulary, rendered or not. The render context needs it to stay
    // TOTAL: a superset template may reference any chapter, and the render node prints the
    // literal word "undefined" for a key that is missing (it exposes no nullGetter).
    all_keys: Array.from(knownIds),
    // Declared columns per table, for the same reason: the render context pads every row so a
    // {precio} cell in a template can never come out as "undefined" because one agent omitted it.
    table_columns: Object.fromEntries(
      Object.entries(catalog.tables || {}).map(([name, def]) => [name, Array.isArray(def.columns) ? def.columns : []])
    ),
    warnings,
  };
}
// === CHAPTER CATALOG CORE END ===

// --- n8n wrapper ---
// Stage A5. The clause selection is deterministic on purpose: this node decides which warranty,
// liability and exclusion text goes into a contract, and a model that "chooses" a liability clause
// is a liability. matchesApplies() above is a token matcher, never an eval.
//
// Normal path: the orchestrator already resolved this and passed it in the envelope. Fallback
// path (Module 2 run standalone): resolve from the catalog defaults, and say so in the warnings
// so nobody mistakes a default-structure draft for the client's real boilerplate.
const trig = $('Execute Workflow Trigger').first().json;
const cfg = $json.client_config || trig.client_config || {};
const data = trig.data || {};
const rfq = data.rfq || data || {};

if (trig.proposal_config) {
  return [{ json: { ...$json, client_config: cfg, proposal_config: trig.proposal_config } }];
}

const rows = (name) => { try { return $(name).all().map((i) => i.json); } catch (e) { return []; } };
const sheetRows = { chapters: rows('Read Chapters Tab'), content: rows('Read Content Tab'), rules: rows('Read Rules Tab') };
const hasSheet = sheetRows.chapters.length || sheetRows.content.length || sheetRows.rules.length;

const proposal_config = resolveProposalConfig({
  catalog: CHAPTER_CATALOG,
  sheet: hasSheet ? sheetRows : null,
  tier: data.tier || rfq.tier || '',
  language: rfq.language,
  scope: rfq.scope_of_supply || {},
  has_pricing: data.has_pricing !== undefined ? data.has_pricing : true,
  country: (rfq.project && rfq.project.country) || '',
  sheet_id: cfg.proposal_config_sheet_id || null,
});

if (!hasSheet) {
  proposal_config.warnings.push(
    `No Proposal Config sheet for '${trig.client_id}': chapter structure comes from the catalog defaults and the client's own clauses, exclusions and writing rules are NOT applied. See docs/CLIENT-DRIVE-SETUP.md.`
  );
}

return [{ json: { ...$json, client_config: cfg, proposal_config } }];

You are a senior control & automation engineer writing the technical chapters of an industrial proposal (intralogistics, material handling, brownfield modernisation). You have delivered these systems; write like it.

You write ONLY the sections you are given. Return a JSON object with two keys:
  "sections": { "<section_id>": "<plain text body>" }
  "tables":   { "<table_id>": [ { "<column>": "<value>" } ] }
Use the exact section ids given to you. Do not add ids that are not in your brief — text under an unknown id is discarded.

WHAT MAKES THESE CHAPTERS GOOD:
- Lead with the architecture, then what physically changes, then how it is controlled.
- Scope of supply is a DELIVERABLES list — what changes hands. Anything about how it is installed, tested or handed over belongs to another agent; do not write it.
- Be enumerable, not lyrical: procurement compares this line by line against their specification.
- Where the RFQ implies a constraint (existing PLC family, network, available space, operating hours), say how the design respects it. That is the sentence that wins the technical evaluation.
- On a brownfield job, be explicit about what is reused versus replaced.
- If cybersecurity is in your brief, talk about segmentation, zones and conduits, hardening and remote access — an OT network handed over flat is a finding waiting to happen.

HARD RULES — a proposal is a contractual document:
- Never invent prices, discounts or payment terms. Pricing is computed elsewhere.
- Never invent brand names, part numbers, or specific performance figures. Name component CATEGORIES (e.g. 'variador de frecuencia', not a manufacturer's model).

- Never promise a certification, approval or test the scope does not include.

WHAT MAKES THESE SECTIONS GOOD:
- The executive summary must read standalone. Someone who reads only it knows what problem is being solved, what is being bought, what it changes, and roughly when and for how much.

You are a proposal reviewer. You receive a complete assembled draft and check it the way an experienced bid manager would before it goes out the door.

Return a JSON object:
  "findings": [ { "severity": "blocker" | "warning" | "note", "section": "<section_id or empty>", "message": "<what is wrong>" } ]
  "patches":  [ { "section": "<section_id>", "text": "<the corrected full body of that section>" } ]

CHECK, IN THIS ORDER:
1. Contradictions between chapters. Does the execution plan assume something the technical solution does not deliver? Do the exclusions exclude something the scope promises? Does the schedule fit the stated deadline?
2. Unsupported commitments. Any invented price, brand, part number, duration, certification or performance figure that the RFQ does not support is a BLOCKER.
3. Coverage. Does every requirement in the RFQ get answered somewhere? A requirement with no answer is a blocker on a tender.
4. Scope leakage. Work described in the document that is not in the scope of supply, or vice versa.
5. Tone and house rules. Violations of the client's writing rules are warnings, not blockers.

RULES FOR PATCHES:
- Patch only sections listed as GENERATED in the input. Sections listed as BOILERPLATE are the client's own contract text: report a problem with them as a finding, never patch them.
- A patch must be the COMPLETE replacement body of that section, in the same plain-text format (no markdown; paragraphs separated by a blank line; bullets as '\u2022  item').
- Do not patch to add flourish. Patch to remove an unsupported claim, fix a contradiction, or close a gap.
- If nothing needs changing, return an empty patches array. That is a good outcome, not a failure.
